speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This Bill introduces two main amendments in relation to stillbirths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have heard their deeply felt sentiments that a stillbirth is similar to the loss of any child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For some parents, being able to officially name the child is an important step in the healing process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In her correspondence, she shared, "official documentation for stillborn babies would afford them a level of dignity commensurate with the impact they had on those who grieved for them" and that it would mean the world to her and her husband if their daughters' legacy would help future bereaved families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The time her twin girls – Abigail and Lara – spent with us may have been short, but they have left an indelible mark in this journey to help the bereaved parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Others had shared their views in an online petition. "For my sleeping child, WY", said one mum.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Another mum said, "Every birth should be recognised, and every baby deserves a name.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In 2007, I lost a baby boy at 24 weeks, and it took me 15 years to finally have another baby." I would also like to mention Ms Felicia Tan, who lost three children and subsequently set up Angel Hearts, a not-for-profit group which creates angel gowns for babies who sadly do not make it home from the hospital.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: She shared that it is heartbreaking for parents to go shopping for suitable wear for burial as the babies are so tiny that even the smallest baby clothing would simply be too big for them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: She said, "Giving the babies a name and clothing them is our way of saying goodbye and remembering them." Another parent reached out to me for a commemorative certificate as they were preparing for a memorial for their stillborn child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We hope the amendments to RBDA to allow for the official registration of a name for a stillborn child will go some way to recognise the birth of the child and support the healing process for bereaved parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Once clause 9 comes into force, there will be a facility for parents to apply to the RG to register a name for the child, within one year after the stillbirth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Subsequently, the digital stillbirth certificate for the child, which can be downloaded from the My Legacy website, will reflect the child's registered name.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The official naming of stillborn children will require enhancements to the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority's (ICA's) systems.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As ICA also has other pressing system enhancements, the enhancement relating to stillbirth naming will take some time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We estimate it to be about two years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The name for a stillborn child will be subject to requirements laid out in the new section 36B, which mirror the requirements for live births.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For instance, the name should not be offensive or obscene.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In the interim, parents who wish to name their stillborn child may apply to ICA for a commemorative birth certificate that reflects the child's name, for remembrance purposes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Currently, "stillborn child" is defined in section 2(1) of RBDA as "a child that issues from the child's mother after the 22nd week of pregnancy and does not show any sign of life at any time after being completely expelled or extracted from the mother." I apologise that this is legal language.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To provide context, RBDA was enacted in 1937 with a definition of stillbirths that used a threshold of 28 weeks of pregnancy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In 2021, when RBDA was repealed and re-enacted, the definition of "stillborn child" was updated to the current threshold of 22 weeks, to align with the World Health Organization's (WHO's) statistical reporting guidelines which recommended using a gestational age of 22 weeks of pregnancy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These guidelines are non-binding on countries and MHA had, in 2021, decided to adopt them for RBDA for consistency with the WHO for the purpose of statistical reporting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Subsequently, MHA received feedback from our local medical community that the threshold of 22 weeks of pregnancy in RBDA may be misinterpreted to be an indication of foetal viability, which refers to the ability of a foetus to survive outside the womb.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Medical practitioners are concerned about this, because local medical and scientific evidence points to 24 weeks of pregnancy as the threshold for foetal viability and not 22 weeks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It is also for this reason that the 24-week threshold is reflected in the Termination of Pregnancy Act 1974, where an abortion is not allowed for a foetus of more than 24 weeks' duration.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Medical practitioners highlighted that if parents mistook the 22-week threshold in RBDA as an indication of foetal viability, there could be confusion for them on the medical interventions for their unborn child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have only had one surviving baby born at 22 weeks in Singapore for the last 10 years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The media reported that the child, a baby girl, was born in 2018 and required a slew of life-sustaining treatments and maximum ventilator support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: She spent a total of 166 days in the hospital before being discharged.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: She is a miracle baby who survived despite the odds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For absolute clarity, clause 2 of the Bill states the existing position that a stillbirth does not include an aborted foetus.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill also makes other amendments, which I will summarise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clauses 3 to 8 of the Bill make amendments to RBDA in relation to registration and re-registration of births.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These amendments are meant for clarity, with no changes to existing processes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clauses 12 to 15 of the Bill make consequential amendments to other Acts, for example, to update the reference to the RBDA 1937, which has been repealed, to the RBDA 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The conversations with bereaved parents, medical practitioners and community partners have been wrought with emotion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Last Friday, as I was settling my younger child to sleep, she suddenly asked if she was a rainbow child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: She had watched an episode on "Bluey", an Australian animated series, on baby loss.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: She reminded me about this rainbow pendant, which was gifted to me by a non-profit organisation, Angel Hearts, last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I hope that today's amendments will help bereaved parents in some way and also remind us that as we treasure and honour our babies who have departed, let us also look to the future with hope.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Ms Mandy Too is now a mother to Josie; and Ms Felicia Tan, a mother to Titus.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I wish all our parents the very best.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that families experiencing this tragic loss can find some solace and closure in naming their babies and as they conduct the necessary rites with these names, laying the babies to rest.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This legislation recognises these babies as beings in their own right – distinguishable from their parents.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: May the names provide their grieving parents a last chance for them to express their hopes and wishes for their children, gone too soon.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I commend the Ministry for considering and fulfilling the wishes of the affected families.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I, therefore, wholeheartedly support this proposed legislation, notwithstanding, there are some pertinent issues for the consideration of the Ministry.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If a baby's stillbirth was due to wrongful conduct, it is important to recognise the tort claim.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The approach may be taken from a legal marker equating foetal life with that of born persons.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The claim would be in alignment with the reproductive justice principles.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The mother is the parent of the child.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: She should not be deprived of the choice for a wrongful death claim.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is consistent with the reproductive justice framework.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It gives a sense of satisfaction that all avenues of investigations have been carried out.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Thirdly, the information from the autopsy may be used during the counselling for future pregnancies.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Fourthly, autopsies enable an improved management approach for future pregnancies.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The mandatory insurance coverage of autopsies after stillbirth would help the women to reduce the costs of the stillbirth.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, the results of autopsies should help to reduce medical costs in future pregnancies, which benefit the women and insurance companies.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These costs may be higher due to any maternal health complications that contributed to the stillbirth.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The parents may incur additional medical costs if they seek mental health treatment.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The parents may also face additional costs related to the child's burial and funeral.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Of course, for the parents of such children, they will always be recognised, regardless of the position of the law.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But the step that this Bill takes, while seemingly small, will confer enormous dignity to these children, who would otherwise have gone on to live a full life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While I cannot fully understand how it feels, as a parent, to lose a child in this manner, my family has experienced the misfortune of a stillborn child.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: As I had previously shared with this House, it was one of the few times that I had seen my father cry – even despite the fact that he was a traditional man.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And it left my mother mourning for years after the loss and still leaves a gaping hole in her heart.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: We had named my brother Jaaron and he would have been 33 years old this year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Had this Bill been in place, we would at least have been able to commemorate him in a formal way and that process would have helped our family find some additional closure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Of course, those who grieve find succour in myriad ways.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: For many, ritual and routine take the mind off the immediacy of the loss, and help the soul heal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: That is why, all across the world, we observe funerals and wakes, and prayers and rites performed for the deceased.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While practices differ – some weep, while others avoid doing so; some are sombre, while others involve singing – the commonality across cultures is that these rituals help with the grieving process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I believe that, for many parents, being able to register the name of their child on birth certificates is one such ritual.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Based on an online petition, this view is also held by more than 2,800 supporters.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It is for this reason – the dignity of recognition that a name confers, which, in turn, helps a mourning family move on from an unspeakable tragedy – that the Workers' Party supports this Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I will offer some additional thoughts on the other stipulations in the Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Ostensibly, this was to conform with the WHO's statistical reporting guidelines.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Based on what I have been able to ascertain, however, the WHO actually recommends – for international comparability – the reporting of late foetal deaths to be at least 28 weeks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is incongruent with the official MHA explanation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: For this reason, I agree with the re-alignment, although I would seek some clarification on why the cutoff was even lowered to 22 weeks in the first place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Presumably, this would be the case, since the birth register is not restricted to only citizens.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Nevertheless, it would be useful to verify that this is the case.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: After all, parental grief is not constrained by their or their stillborn child's national origin.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I wish to close with a more general lesson from this episode.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While the Ministry has suggested that it has been looking to refine the laws in this regard since 2022, in response to two separate Parliamentary Questions I filed that year gave little indication that there was any intention to change the law.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The first, in May, simply stated that, "birth certificates are not issued to stillbirths" and suggested that MHA would stop at the stage of issuing a "digital stillbirth certificate".

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The second, in September that year, stressed the need for, "process and system changes," some of which Minister of State Sun had elaborated on but, likewise, seemed unnecessarily dismissive, bluntly declaring that ICA had "received only one request" for a commemorative birth certificate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This response prompted my suggestion to Mandy Too and Aidan Hoy, the parents of Abigail and Lara, that if there was a way to demonstrate that birth certificates for stillborns was a matter that had broad support, it may help move the needle in the direction of change.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And to their enormous credit, Ms Too and Mr Hoy did the rest: they gathered the signatures and support to advocate for this cause.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I think this episode is a reminder for all of us, that the power to effect change, ultimately, lies within our hands.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Representatives like those in this House are often only a conduit for the desires of our people to shape the world that we live in.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: When ordinary people have the courage to act on their convictions, change happens.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: That is the power of the people, in a democratic society.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is an empathetic move that gives due acknowledgment to the lived, personal experiences of Singaporeans who have had the misfortune of losing their child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first clarification is on the concern of misinterpretation of the stillborn threshold in the Registration of Births and Deaths Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The feedback was that the stillborn threshold may be misinterpreted as an indication of foetal viability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This may confuse parents making difficult decisions about medical interventions for their unborn children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Additionally, there were concerns expressed that such ambiguities lead to pressure on medical practitioners to use treatment methods that may increase the risk of severe neurodevelopmental disabilities in infants who survive or in higher rates of futile resuscitation attempts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Increasing the threshold is one way to remove potentially confusing information.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But it will not fully solve the problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is even more important to ensure that parents have accurate, scientific information to help them make emotionally-charged decisions on foetal viability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second set of clarifications is on the naming of the stillborn child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister of State share if parents, whose stillborn are birthed in this transition period before the provisions are operationalised, can apply for their stillborn child to be named once the provisions come into effect?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister of State also confirm that steps will be taken to ensure that the application process for entering a name for the stillborn will be sensitively designed and easy for parents to navigate?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Please allow me to address the questions and feedback in turn.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether parents can officially register a name for stillbirths that occur during the transition period before the provisions are operationalised.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This time limit also applies to parents who have had stillborn children before the legal provisions are operationalised.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I would also like to assure Mr Ng that ICA will ensure that the application process is sensitively designed and easy to navigate.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Ng also asked about the steps that the Government is taking to ensure that parents have accurate, scientific information on foetal viability outside the womb.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When parents are faced with the prospect of delivery before the infant is at full term, they will be counselled by their doctors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This includes information on the infant's chances of survival and risk of severe complications, and takes into account the specifics of the case, such as any medical conditions the mother may have.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Such counselling will help parents to come to an informed decision about the appropriate course of medical intervention.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Gan also asked the Government to consider mandatory insurance coverage for autopsies after stillbirths.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Autopsy, or post-mortem examination, is not routinely offered for stillbirths and the decision on an autopsy of a stillborn child is a personal decision by the parent.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As this is a personal decision by the parent, parents may seek their own options to cover the cost.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh also asked about the practical assistance and support that could be provided to parents to cover the costs associated with the stillbirth.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We recognise that we need to support parents of stillborns.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our public maternity hospitals provide support for these parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Parents may also be referred to a medical social worker, nurse or mental health team for emotional and practical support, such as advice on financial assistance and counselling during the bereavement process.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In the Government's desire to support families and employees, there is also continuous engagement with employers and employees to look at how leave benefits can support better work-life situations, better productivity in the workplace and better overall well-being for employees.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When MHA and the Government look into reviews, we do not look at it cursorily.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And when we say we will study something, we will commit to it and study it carefully before committing to policy and legislative changes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As you would know, by October 2023, our systems were in place to start issuance of commemorative birth certificates.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And the first certificates were issued to Ms Mandy Too's twin daughters.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We were also careful with publicity as we do not want to make it look like it was compulsory and different parents may also address infant loss differently.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When ICA and MHA undertake to look into policy change and effect legislative change, we make sure that we tackle all the nuts and bolts so that when we decide to go ahead with these changes, we are able to meet the needs of bereaved parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: The Chairman
text: The citation year "2023" will be changed to "2024", as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.
